source: HCAI Hospital Annual Financial Data Selected Data File Documentation (report periods ended on/after 6/30/2004)

sections.title: Report information
sections.summary: Which report the numbers came from and how complete it is.

sections.title: Hospital profile
sections.summary: Who the hospital is: location, ownership, type, and designations.

sections.title: Beds & capacity
sections.summary: How many beds the hospital is licensed for, has available, and actually staffs.
drivers: License changes: beds added, closed, or converted to another type of care.
Seismic retrofits or construction taking units out of service (California SB 1953 requirements).
Staffed beds track staffing availability — nursing shortages reduce staffed beds without changing the license.

sections.title: Inpatient volume by payer
sections.summary: Patient days and discharges split by who is responsible for the bill.
drivers: Admission volume: service-line growth, physician recruitment or departures, a competitor opening or closing.
Length of stay: delays discharging patients to skilled nursing or home care add days without adding patients.

Payer shifts: Medicare Advantage growth moves volume from Medicare fee-for-service to Medicare managed care; Medi-Cal enrollment swings (the 2023–24 end of continuous coverage, the 2024 expansion to undocumented adults) move volume between Medi-Cal, county programs, and self-pay.
Partial reporting periods (opening, closure, fiscal-year change) — check Days in Report Period.

sections.title: Beds & volume by type of care
sections.summary: Beds, patient days, and discharges for acute, psychiatric, rehab, long-term care, and other units.
drivers: Opening, closing, or converting a unit (e.g., closing a psych unit or skilled nursing unit).
Changes in length of stay or referral patterns for that service line.
Internal transfers between types of care count as a discharge from one and an admission to the other.

sections.title: Occupancy & length of stay
sections.summary: How full the hospital is and how long patients stay.
drivers: Occupancy moves with patient days (numerator) and bed counts (denominator) — a bed closure raises occupancy with no change in volume.
Length of stay rises when discharges to post-acute care are delayed or case mix gets sicker; it falls with care-management programs.

sections.title: Nursery
sections.summary: Newborn nursery capacity and volume (kept separate from inpatient beds and days).
drivers: Birth volume in the service area (California births have been declining).
Obstetric unit openings or closures — many smaller and rural hospitals have closed labor & delivery.

sections.title: Outpatient visits by payer
sections.summary: Outpatient visits split by who is responsible for the bill.
drivers: Care continuing to shift from inpatient to outpatient settings.
Opening, acquiring, or closing clinics and satellite sites that report under the hospital license.
Payer shifts (Medicare Advantage growth, Medi-Cal enrollment changes).
Changes in how visits are counted; telehealth may not be counted as a visit.

sections.title: Emergency & outpatient visits
sections.summary: Visits by setting: emergency department, clinics, home health, and referred outpatient services.
drivers: ED volume swings with respiratory-virus seasons, the 2020 COVID drop, and nearby urgent-care or ED openings/closures.
Clinic volume moves with sites being added, sold, or moved to an affiliated medical group.

sections.title: Surgery & births
sections.summary: Operating rooms, surgical volume, and deliveries.
drivers: Surgeon recruitment or departures and new or lost payer contracts.
Procedures migrating to freestanding ambulatory surgery centers.
Elective-surgery pauses (e.g., 2020 COVID restrictions, staffing shortages).

sections.title: Income statement
sections.summary: The top-line P&L: revenue, expenses, and the resulting margin.
drivers: Volume and payment-rate changes (annual Medicare updates, commercial contract renegotiations).
Medi-Cal supplemental payments such as the Hospital Quality Assurance Fee program arrive in lumpy, multi-year cycles and can swing results sharply year to year.
Labor costs: the 2021–22 travel-nurse surge and California's health care worker minimum wage (SB 525, phased in from October 2024).
One-time items: COVID relief grants in 2020–21, prior-year cost report settlements.

sections.title: Gross revenue by service
sections.summary: Charges at full list price, split into inpatient room & board, ambulatory, and ancillary services.
drivers: Annual chargemaster (list price) increases — gross charges rise even when volume is flat.
Volume and acuity changes in each service group.
sections.caution: Gross charges are list prices that almost no payer pays. Use net patient revenue to judge real change or compare hospitals.

sections.title: Gross inpatient revenue by payer
sections.summary: Inpatient charges at full list price, by payer.
drivers: Annual chargemaster increases.
Inpatient volume and case mix by payer.
Payer shifts such as Medicare fee-for-service to Medicare Advantage.
sections.caution: Gross charges are list prices, not what the hospital collects. They're most useful as a consistent way to measure payer mix.

sections.title: Gross outpatient revenue by payer
sections.summary: Outpatient charges at full list price, by payer.
drivers: Annual chargemaster increases.
Outpatient volume growth as care shifts out of the hospital bed.
Payer shifts such as Medicare fee-for-service to Medicare Advantage.
sections.caution: Gross charges are list prices, not what the hospital collects. They're most useful as a consistent way to measure payer mix.

sections.title: Deductions from revenue
sections.summary: The gap between list-price charges and what the hospital expects to collect.
drivers: Chargemaster increases widen contractual adjustments automatically (list price rises faster than payment).
Payer contract terms and payer mix.
Some Medi-Cal supplemental payments are recorded as reductions to Medi-Cal contractual adjustments, so these lines can swing with supplemental payment timing.
Charity-care and bad-debt policy changes, and patients gaining or losing coverage.

sections.title: Capitation revenue
sections.summary: Fixed per-member-per-month payments from managed care plans, regardless of services used.
drivers: Contracts moving between capitated and fee-for-service arrangements.
Changes in the number of members assigned under capitated contracts.

sections.title: Net patient revenue by payer
sections.summary: What the hospital actually expects to collect, by payer.
drivers: Payment-rate changes: annual Medicare rate updates, commercial contract renegotiations, Medi-Cal rate actions.
Volume and payer-mix shifts.
Medi-Cal supplemental payments (Hospital Quality Assurance Fee program, disproportionate share) — timing can make one year look unusually strong or weak.
Prior-year settlements with Medicare or Medi-Cal booked in the current year.

sections.title: Other financial items
sections.summary: Transfers, contributions, investment income, and public funding outside patient care.
drivers: Investment market performance (e.g., losses in 2022, recovery in 2023).
Fundraising and one-time gifts.
District tax revenue or county appropriations for public hospitals.
Cash moved to or from a parent organization.

sections.title: Expenses by department group
sections.summary: Operating expenses assigned to the part of the hospital that incurred them.
drivers: Volume in that service group, staffing levels, and wage rates.
Cost-allocation or chart-of-accounts changes can move dollars between groups without changing the total.

sections.title: Expenses by type
sections.summary: Operating expenses by what was bought: labor, supplies, services, capital.
drivers: Wage rates, headcount, and union contracts.
Supply and drug price inflation, and changes in case mix.
Outsourcing decisions move cost between salaries and purchased services.

sections.title: Balance sheet — assets
sections.summary: What the hospital owns at the end of the period.
drivers: Operating results adding to or draining cash.
Capital projects: construction in progress becomes buildings and equipment when finished.
Cash swept to or from a parent system.
sections.caution: These are hospital-level balance sheets. Hospitals in a health system often keep cash and debt at the parent, so hospital-level figures can understate the system's real financial position.

sections.title: Balance sheet — liabilities & equity
sections.summary: What the hospital owes and the net worth left over.
drivers: New debt or refinancing (often for seismic compliance or expansion).
Operating gains or losses flowing into equity.
Debt pushed down from, or taken up by, a parent organization.
sections.caution: These are hospital-level balance sheets. Hospitals in a health system often keep cash and debt at the parent, so hospital-level figures can understate the system's real financial position.

sections.title: Balance sheet — detail
sections.summary: Selected balance sheet line items: cash, receivables, property, and debt detail.
drivers: Collection performance, claim denials, and billing-system conversions change receivables.
New buildings, equipment, and depreciation change property values.
Bond issues, refinancing, and scheduled principal payments change debt.
sections.caution: These are hospital-level balance sheets. Hospitals in a health system often keep cash and debt at the parent, so hospital-level figures can understate the system's real financial position.

sections.title: Workforce
sections.summary: Paid staff, hours, medical staff, and trainees.
drivers: Volume and California's mandated nurse-to-patient ratios.
Replacing contract (registry/travel) staff with employees, or the reverse.
Outsourcing departments such as food service or environmental services.

sections.title: Hours worked by job category
sections.summary: Hours actually worked, by employee classification.
drivers: Staffing levels and mix (e.g., more RNs vs. LVNs or aides).
Volume changes and new or closed services.

sections.title: Contract labor
sections.summary: Hours worked by staff not on the hospital payroll (registry/travel nurses, contractors).
drivers: Contract labor surged in 2021–22 during COVID-era nursing shortages and has generally declined since.
Vacancy rates and success of hiring and retention programs.

sections.title: Hours worked by department group
sections.summary: Hours actually worked (productive hours), by department group.
drivers: Volume and staffing in each department group.
Departments being outsourced, consolidated to a parent system, or brought in-house.

sections.title: Paid hours by department group
sections.summary: Hours paid, including vacation, sick, and holiday time, by department group.
drivers: Staffing levels plus paid-time-off policies and usage.
Departments being outsourced, consolidated to a parent system, or brought in-house.

fields.label: HCAI facility ID
fields.summary: HCAI's nine-digit ID for the hospital license. Stays the same even if the hospital's name changes.

fields.label: Hospital name
fields.summary: The name the hospital does business under.

fields.label: Report start date
fields.summary: First day covered by this report.

fields.label: Report end date
fields.summary: Last day covered by this report — normally the hospital's fiscal year end.

fields.label: Days covered
fields.summary: Number of days this report covers. Usually 365; anything else means the hospital opened, closed, changed owners, or changed its fiscal year.
fields.caution: Short or long periods make volumes and dollars look unusually low or high. This app annualizes them when combining reports.

fields.label: Audit status
fields.summary: 'Audited' means HCAI finished its desk review; 'In Process' means the numbers may still change.

fields.label: Includes auditor adjustments?
fields.summary: Whether the report includes adjustments from the hospital's independent financial audit.

fields.label: County
fields.summary: County where the hospital is located.

fields.label: Health service area
fields.summary: One of California's 14 federally designated health planning regions (e.g., 11 = Los Angeles County).

fields.label: Planning area
fields.summary: HCAI's smaller planning area within the health service area, used to assess local bed need.

fields.label: Ownership type
fields.summary: Who owns and governs the hospital: Non-Profit, Investor (for-profit), District, City/County, or State.

fields.label: Primary type of care
fields.summary: The hospital's main focus: General acute, Children's, Psychiatric, or Specialty.

fields.label: Comparability group
fields.summary: Whether HCAI considers the hospital's data comparable to typical hospitals. Kaiser, psychiatric health facilities, state hospitals, and long-term-care-focused hospitals are flagged separately.
fields.caution: Kaiser hospitals report financials differently from other hospitals, so this app leaves non-comparable hospitals out of peer groups by default.

fields.label: Teaching or rural status
fields.summary: Marks HCAI-designated teaching hospitals and small/rural hospitals (per Health & Safety Code §124840).

fields.label: Phone
fields.summary: Main business phone number.

fields.label: Address
fields.summary: Street address of the hospital.

fields.label: City
fields.summary: City where the hospital is located.

fields.label: ZIP code
fields.summary: Hospital ZIP code.

fields.label: CEO
fields.summary: The hospital's chief executive or top administrator at the time of the report.

fields.label: CEO title
fields.summary: Title of the top executive.

fields.label: Website
fields.summary: Hospital website.

fields.label: Licensed owner
fields.summary: The organization licensed to operate the hospital, often the parent health system.

fields.label: Report preparer
fields.summary: Person who prepared the annual disclosure report.

fields.label: Preparer's organization
fields.summary: Organization of the person who prepared the report.

fields.label: Trauma center level
fields.summary: Trauma designation from the local EMS agency. Level I is the highest; blank means not a designated trauma center.

fields.label: Medicare provider number (CCN)
fields.summary: Medicare certification number, useful for matching to CMS datasets.

fields.label: Medi-Cal contract provider number
fields.summary: Medi-Cal provider number used for contracted services.

fields.label: Medi-Cal non-contract provider number
fields.summary: Medi-Cal provider number used for non-contracted services.

fields.label: Licensed beds
fields.summary: Beds on the hospital's license at period end (not counting newborn bassinets). The usual measure of hospital size.

fields.label: Available beds
fields.summary: Average number of beds physically in place and usable, whether or not staffed.

fields.label: Staffed beds
fields.summary: Average number of beds set up and staffed for patients — the beds the hospital can actually use.

fields.label: Patient days — Medicare fee-for-service
fields.summary: Inpatient days for traditional Medicare, billed directly to the federal program. Each patient in a bed at the midnight census counts as one day.

fields.label: Patient days — Medicare Advantage
fields.summary: Inpatient days for medicare beneficiaries enrolled in a private Medicare Advantage (managed care) plan. Each patient in a bed at the midnight census counts as one day.

fields.label: Patient days — Medi-Cal fee-for-service
fields.summary: Inpatient days for medi-Cal (California Medicaid) billed directly to the state, not through a health plan. Each patient in a bed at the midnight census counts as one day.

fields.label: Patient days — Medi-Cal managed care
fields.summary: Inpatient days for medi-Cal members enrolled in a managed care plan, which covers most Medi-Cal enrollees. Each patient in a bed at the midnight census counts as one day.

fields.hcaiLabel: Patient (Census) Days County Indigent Programs-Traditional & Managed Care
fields.label: Patient days — County indigent programs
fields.summary: Inpatient days for low-income patients covered by county programs, traditional and managed care. Each patient in a bed at the midnight census counts as one day.

fields.label: Patient days — Commercial & other, non-managed
fields.summary: Inpatient days for other coverage without a managed-care contract: indemnity plans, workers' comp, TRICARE, California Children's Services. Each patient in a bed at the midnight census counts as one day.

fields.hcaiLabel: Patient (Census) Days Other Third Parties-Managed Care
fields.label: Patient days — Commercial managed care
fields.summary: Inpatient days for private HMO/PPO plans not funded by Medicare, Medi-Cal, or a county. Each patient in a bed at the midnight census counts as one day.

fields.label: Patient days — Other indigent (charity)
fields.summary: Inpatient days for patients receiving charity care from the hospital outside county programs. Each patient in a bed at the midnight census counts as one day.

fields.label: Patient days — Self-pay & other
fields.summary: Inpatient days for everyone not in another category, mostly self-pay and uninsured patients. Each patient in a bed at the midnight census counts as one day.

fields.label: Patient days — All payers
fields.summary: Inpatient days for total across all payer categories. Each patient in a bed at the midnight census counts as one day.

fields.label: Discharges — Medicare fee-for-service
fields.summary: Inpatients released from the hospital (including deaths) for traditional Medicare, billed directly to the federal program. Roughly, the number of inpatient stays.

fields.label: Discharges — Medicare Advantage
fields.summary: Inpatients released from the hospital (including deaths) for medicare beneficiaries enrolled in a private Medicare Advantage (managed care) plan. Roughly, the number of inpatient stays.

fields.label: Discharges — Medi-Cal fee-for-service
fields.summary: Inpatients released from the hospital (including deaths) for medi-Cal (California Medicaid) billed directly to the state, not through a health plan. Roughly, the number of inpatient stays.

fields.label: Discharges — Medi-Cal managed care
fields.summary: Inpatients released from the hospital (including deaths) for medi-Cal members enrolled in a managed care plan, which covers most Medi-Cal enrollees. Roughly, the number of inpatient stays.

fields.hcaiLabel: Discharges County Indigent Programs-Traditional & Managed Care
fields.label: Discharges — County indigent programs
fields.summary: Inpatients released from the hospital (including deaths) for low-income patients covered by county programs, traditional and managed care. Roughly, the number of inpatient stays.

fields.label: Discharges — Commercial & other, non-managed
fields.summary: Inpatients released from the hospital (including deaths) for other coverage without a managed-care contract: indemnity plans, workers' comp, TRICARE, California Children's Services. Roughly, the number of inpatient stays.

fields.label: Discharges — Commercial managed care
fields.summary: Inpatients released from the hospital (including deaths) for private HMO/PPO plans not funded by Medicare, Medi-Cal, or a county. Roughly, the number of inpatient stays.

fields.label: Discharges — Other indigent (charity)
fields.summary: Inpatients released from the hospital (including deaths) for patients receiving charity care from the hospital outside county programs. Roughly, the number of inpatient stays.

fields.label: Discharges — Self-pay & other
fields.summary: Inpatients released from the hospital (including deaths) for everyone not in another category, mostly self-pay and uninsured patients. Roughly, the number of inpatient stays.

fields.label: Discharges — All payers
fields.summary: Inpatients released from the hospital (including deaths) for total across all payer categories. Roughly, the number of inpatient stays.

fields.label: Acute care licensed beds
fields.summary: Licensed beds in general acute units: medical/surgical, ICU, obstetrics, pediatrics.

fields.label: Psychiatric licensed beds
fields.summary: Licensed beds in inpatient psychiatric units.

fields.label: Chemical dependency licensed beds
fields.summary: Licensed beds in chemical dependency (substance use) recovery units.

fields.label: Rehabilitation licensed beds
fields.summary: Licensed beds in physical rehabilitation units.

fields.label: Long-term care licensed beds
fields.summary: Licensed beds in skilled nursing, sub-acute, and intermediate care units.

fields.hcaiLabel: Licensed Beds Residential & Other Daily Services
fields.label: Residential & other licensed beds
fields.summary: Licensed beds in residential care and other daily services.

fields.label: Acute care patient days
fields.summary: Inpatient days in general acute units: medical/surgical, ICU, obstetrics, pediatrics.

fields.label: Psychiatric patient days
fields.summary: Inpatient days in inpatient psychiatric units.

fields.label: Chemical dependency patient days
fields.summary: Inpatient days in chemical dependency (substance use) recovery units.

fields.label: Rehabilitation patient days
fields.summary: Inpatient days in physical rehabilitation units.

fields.label: Long-term care patient days
fields.summary: Inpatient days in skilled nursing, sub-acute, and intermediate care units.

fields.hcaiLabel: Patient (Census) Days Residential & Other Daily Services
fields.label: Residential & other patient days
fields.summary: Inpatient days in residential care and other daily services.

fields.label: Acute care discharges
fields.summary: Discharges from general acute units: medical/surgical, ICU, obstetrics, pediatrics, including transfers to another type of care in the hospital.

fields.label: Psychiatric discharges
fields.summary: Discharges from inpatient psychiatric units, including transfers to another type of care in the hospital.

fields.label: Chemical dependency discharges
fields.summary: Discharges from chemical dependency (substance use) recovery units, including transfers to another type of care in the hospital.

fields.label: Rehabilitation discharges
fields.summary: Discharges from physical rehabilitation units, including transfers to another type of care in the hospital.

fields.label: Long-term care discharges
fields.summary: Discharges from skilled nursing, sub-acute, and intermediate care units, including transfers to another type of care in the hospital.

fields.label: Residential & other discharges
fields.summary: Discharges from residential care and other daily services, including transfers to another type of care in the hospital.

fields.label: Occupancy (licensed beds)
fields.summary: Share of licensed bed capacity that was filled: patient days ÷ (licensed beds × days in period).
fields.caution: Licensed beds often exceed staffed beds, so this can understate how full the hospital feels day to day.

fields.label: Occupancy (available beds)
fields.summary: Share of available bed capacity that was filled: patient days ÷ (available beds × days in period).

fields.label: Average length of stay (all units)
fields.summary: Average days per inpatient stay, including long-term care units.
fields.caution: Long-term care stays are much longer, so hospitals with skilled nursing units look higher. Use the 'excluding LTC' version to compare.

fields.label: Average length of stay (excl. long-term care)
fields.summary: Average days per inpatient stay, excluding long-term care units. The more comparable version.

fields.label: Nursery bassinets
fields.summary: Average number of newborn nursery bassinets.

fields.label: Nursery days
fields.summary: Days newborns spent in the regular nursery (not NICU).

fields.label: Nursery discharges
fields.summary: Newborns released from the regular nursery.

fields.label: Outpatient visits — Medicare fee-for-service
fields.summary: Outpatient visits (ED, clinic, referred, home health) for traditional Medicare, billed directly to the federal program.

fields.label: Outpatient visits — Medicare Advantage
fields.summary: Outpatient visits (ED, clinic, referred, home health) for medicare beneficiaries enrolled in a private Medicare Advantage (managed care) plan.

fields.label: Outpatient visits — Medi-Cal fee-for-service
fields.summary: Outpatient visits (ED, clinic, referred, home health) for medi-Cal (California Medicaid) billed directly to the state, not through a health plan.

fields.label: Outpatient visits — Medi-Cal managed care
fields.summary: Outpatient visits (ED, clinic, referred, home health) for medi-Cal members enrolled in a managed care plan, which covers most Medi-Cal enrollees.

fields.hcaiLabel: Outpatient Visits County Indigent Programs-Traditional & Managed Care
fields.label: Outpatient visits — County indigent programs
fields.summary: Outpatient visits (ED, clinic, referred, home health) for low-income patients covered by county programs, traditional and managed care.

fields.label: Outpatient visits — Commercial & other, non-managed
fields.summary: Outpatient visits (ED, clinic, referred, home health) for other coverage without a managed-care contract: indemnity plans, workers' comp, TRICARE, California Children's Services.

fields.hcaiLabel: Outpatient Visits Other Third Parties-Managed Care
fields.label: Outpatient visits — Commercial managed care
fields.summary: Outpatient visits (ED, clinic, referred, home health) for private HMO/PPO plans not funded by Medicare, Medi-Cal, or a county.

fields.label: Outpatient visits — Other indigent (charity)
fields.summary: Outpatient visits (ED, clinic, referred, home health) for patients receiving charity care from the hospital outside county programs.

fields.label: Outpatient visits — Self-pay & other
fields.summary: Outpatient visits (ED, clinic, referred, home health) for everyone not in another category, mostly self-pay and uninsured patients.

fields.label: Outpatient visits — All payers
fields.summary: Outpatient visits (ED, clinic, referred, home health) for total across all payer categories.

fields.label: Emergency department visits
fields.summary: Every patient visit to the emergency department, whether or not the patient was then admitted.

fields.label: Clinic visits
fields.summary: Scheduled visits to the hospital's on-site or satellite clinics.

fields.label: Home health visits
fields.summary: Visits by the hospital's home health staff to patients' homes.

fields.label: Referred outpatient visits
fields.summary: Visits by patients sent by an outside physician for tests or therapy (e.g., imaging, lab, physical therapy).

fields.label: Purchased inpatient days
fields.summary: Inpatient days the hospital bought from another hospital for its managed care members.

fields.label: Operating rooms
fields.summary: Operating rooms at the hospital and its satellite surgery centers.

fields.label: Inpatient operating minutes
fields.summary: Total minutes of inpatient surgery, measured from start to end of anesthesia.

fields.label: Outpatient operating minutes
fields.summary: Total minutes of outpatient surgery, measured from start to end of anesthesia.

fields.label: Inpatient surgeries
fields.summary: Inpatient surgical cases. One patient visit counts as one surgery regardless of procedures performed.

fields.label: Outpatient surgeries
fields.summary: Same-day outpatient surgical cases.

fields.label: Vaginal births
fields.summary: Babies delivered without surgery.

fields.label: C-sections
fields.summary: Babies delivered by cesarean section.

fields.label: Gross patient revenue (charges)
fields.summary: All patient charges at full list price, before any discounts.
fields.caution: List prices, not collections. Rises every year with price increases even when volume is flat.

fields.label: Total deductions from revenue
fields.summary: All reductions from list price: contractual discounts, charity care, bad debt, and other adjustments.

fields.label: Capitation revenue
fields.summary: Fixed per-member-per-month payments from managed care plans.

fields.label: Net patient revenue
fields.summary: What the hospital expects to actually collect for patient care: charges + capitation − deductions. The best single measure of patient revenue.

fields.label: Other operating revenue
fields.summary: Revenue from non-patient activities tied to operations, such as cafeteria sales, parking, and rebates.
drivers: Grant income (some hospitals booked COVID relief funds here in 2020–21).
New or discontinued retail pharmacy, cafeteria, or parking operations.

fields.label: Total operating expenses
fields.summary: The full cost of running the hospital: labor, supplies, services, depreciation, and interest. Excludes bad debt.

fields.label: Operating income
fields.summary: Operating revenue minus operating expenses — profit or loss from running the hospital, before investment income and other non-operating items.

fields.label: Non-operating revenue
fields.summary: Income not tied to patient care: investment returns, donations, district taxes, county appropriations.
drivers: Investment market swings (e.g., 2022 losses, 2023 recovery).
One-time gifts or asset sales.

fields.label: Non-operating expenses
fields.summary: Costs not tied to patient care, such as running a medical office building or gift shop.

fields.label: Income taxes
fields.summary: Income taxes. Only for investor-owned hospitals.

fields.label: Extraordinary items
fields.summary: Rare, one-time gains or losses (e.g., a fire). Positive = loss, negative = gain.

fields.label: Net income (bottom line)
fields.summary: Operating income plus non-operating items, minus taxes and extraordinary items.
fields.caution: Can be driven by investment returns rather than operations. Look at operating income for the underlying business.

fields.hcaiLabel: Gross Outpatient Revenue Other Third Parties-Managed Care
fields.label: Outpatient charges — Commercial managed care
fields.summary: Outpatient charges at full list price for private HMO/PPO plans not funded by Medicare, Medi-Cal, or a county, before discounts.

fields.label: Outpatient charges — Other indigent (charity)
fields.summary: Outpatient charges at full list price for patients receiving charity care from the hospital outside county programs, before discounts.

fields.label: Outpatient charges — Self-pay & other
fields.summary: Outpatient charges at full list price for everyone not in another category, mostly self-pay and uninsured patients, before discounts.

fields.label: Outpatient charges — All payers
fields.summary: Outpatient charges at full list price for total across all payer categories, before discounts.

fields.label: Contractual discount — Medicare fee-for-service
fields.summary: The discount from list price that the hospital gives under its contract terms for traditional Medicare, billed directly to the federal program.

fields.label: Contractual discount — Medicare Advantage
fields.summary: The discount from list price that the hospital gives under its contract terms for medicare beneficiaries enrolled in a private Medicare Advantage (managed care) plan.

fields.label: Contractual discount — Medi-Cal fee-for-service
fields.summary: The discount from list price that the hospital gives under its contract terms for medi-Cal (California Medicaid) billed directly to the state, not through a health plan.

fields.label: Contractual discount — Medi-Cal managed care
fields.summary: The discount from list price that the hospital gives under its contract terms for medi-Cal members enrolled in a managed care plan, which covers most Medi-Cal enrollees.

fields.label: Medi-Cal DSH payments (SB 855)
fields.summary: Extra Medi-Cal payments to hospitals serving many low-income patients. Recorded as a negative deduction (it adds revenue).
drivers: Eligibility and payment amounts are recalculated each program year.
Timing of state payments can shift amounts between years.

fields.hcaiLabel: Contractual Adjustments County Indigent Programs-Traditional & Managed Care
fields.label: Contractual discount — County indigent programs
fields.summary: The discount from list price that the hospital gives under its contract terms for low-income patients covered by county programs, traditional and managed care.

fields.label: Contractual discount — Commercial & other, non-managed
fields.summary: The discount from list price that the hospital gives under its contract terms for other coverage without a managed-care contract: indemnity plans, workers' comp, TRICARE, California Children's Services.

fields.hcaiLabel: Contractual Adjustments Other Third Parties-Managed Care
fields.label: Contractual discount — Commercial managed care
fields.summary: The discount from list price that the hospital gives under its contract terms for private HMO/PPO plans not funded by Medicare, Medi-Cal, or a county.

fields.label: Bad debt
fields.summary: Bills the hospital expects patients who could pay won't pay.
drivers: Patients losing coverage (e.g., Medi-Cal redeterminations in 2023–24) or rising deductibles.
Changes in how accounts are classified between bad debt and charity care.

fields.label: Charity care (Hill-Burton)
fields.summary: Free or reduced-price care provided to meet federal Hill-Burton obligations. Rare today.

fields.label: Charity care
fields.summary: Care provided free or at a discount to patients unable to pay, valued at list price.
drivers: Financial assistance policy changes (California's AB 1020 expanded eligibility starting 2024).
Changes in the uninsured population and Medi-Cal enrollment.

fields.hcaiLabel: Restricted Donations and Subsidies for Indigent Care
fields.label: Donations & subsidies for indigent care
fields.summary: Grants or subsidies designated for indigent patients' care. Recorded as a negative deduction.

fields.label: Other deductions
fields.summary: Other reductions from charges: policy discounts, administrative adjustments, and teaching allowances at UC hospitals.

fields.label: Capitation revenue — Medicare Advantage
fields.summary: Fixed per-member-per-month payments from Medicare Advantage plans.

fields.label: Capitation revenue — Medi-Cal managed care
fields.summary: Fixed per-member-per-month payments from Medi-Cal managed care plans.

fields.hcaiLabel: Capitation Premium Revenue County Indigent Programs-Managed Care
fields.label: Capitation revenue — county indigent managed care
fields.summary: Fixed per-member-per-month payments from county indigent managed care plans.

fields.hcaiLabel: Capitation Premium Revenue Other Third Parties-Managed Care
fields.label: Capitation revenue — commercial managed care
fields.summary: Fixed per-member-per-month payments from commercial managed care plans.

fields.label: Net patient revenue — Medicare fee-for-service
fields.summary: What the hospital expects to collect for traditional Medicare, billed directly to the federal program, after discounts.

fields.label: Net patient revenue — Medicare Advantage
fields.summary: What the hospital expects to collect for medicare beneficiaries enrolled in a private Medicare Advantage (managed care) plan, after discounts.

fields.label: Net patient revenue — Medi-Cal fee-for-service
fields.summary: What the hospital expects to collect for medi-Cal (California Medicaid) billed directly to the state, not through a health plan, after discounts.

fields.label: Net patient revenue — Medi-Cal managed care
fields.summary: What the hospital expects to collect for medi-Cal members enrolled in a managed care plan, which covers most Medi-Cal enrollees, after discounts.

fields.hcaiLabel: Net Patient Revenue County Indigent Programs-Traditional & Managed Care
fields.label: Net patient revenue — County indigent programs
fields.summary: What the hospital expects to collect for low-income patients covered by county programs, traditional and managed care, after discounts.

fields.hcaiLabel: Net Patient Revenue Other Third Parties-Traditional
fields.label: Net patient revenue — Commercial & other, non-managed
fields.summary: What the hospital expects to collect for other coverage without a managed-care contract: indemnity plans, workers' comp, TRICARE, California Children's Services, after discounts.

fields.hcaiLabel: Net Patient Revenue Other Third Parties-Managed Care
fields.label: Net patient revenue — Commercial managed care
fields.summary: What the hospital expects to collect for private HMO/PPO plans not funded by Medicare, Medi-Cal, or a county, after discounts.

fields.label: Net patient revenue — Other indigent (charity)
fields.summary: What the hospital expects to collect for patients receiving charity care from the hospital outside county programs, after discounts.

fields.label: Net patient revenue — Self-pay & other
fields.summary: What the hospital expects to collect for everyone not in another category, mostly self-pay and uninsured patients, after discounts.

fields.hcaiLabel: Dispro Share Funds Transferred to Related Public Entity
fields.label: DSH funds transferred out
fields.summary: Medi-Cal disproportionate share funds a public hospital passed back to a related public entity.

fields.label: Transfers with parent/affiliates
fields.summary: Cash sent to (negative) or received from (positive) a related organization. Affects equity directly.

fields.label: Unrestricted donations
fields.summary: Gifts and grants with no donor restrictions.

fields.hcaiLabel: Incomes, Gains & Losses from Unrestricted Investments
fields.label: Investment income
fields.summary: Interest, dividends, and gains or losses on unrestricted investments.

fields.label: District tax revenue
fields.summary: Property-tax and assessment revenue received by healthcare district hospitals.

fields.label: County appropriations
fields.summary: General-fund support a county provides to its county hospital.

fields.label: Inpatient unit expenses
fields.summary: Direct costs of inpatient nursing units.

fields.label: Ambulatory expenses
fields.summary: Direct costs of the ED, clinics, observation, and home health.

fields.label: Ancillary expenses
fields.summary: Direct costs of lab, imaging, pharmacy, surgery, therapy, and other ancillary departments.

fields.label: Purchased inpatient care
fields.summary: Cost of inpatient care bought from other hospitals for managed care members.

fields.label: Purchased outpatient care
fields.summary: Cost of outpatient care bought from other hospitals, usually under capitation contracts.

fields.label: Research expenses
fields.summary: Direct costs of formal research programs.

fields.label: Education expenses
fields.summary: Direct costs of formal education programs such as residency and nursing school (not in-service training).

fields.label: General services expenses
fields.summary: Dietary, laundry, housekeeping, and plant operations.

fields.label: Fiscal services expenses
fields.summary: Accounting, patient accounting (billing), and admitting.

fields.label: Administrative expenses
fields.summary: Administration, HR, medical records, and similar overhead departments.
drivers: Management fees charged by a parent health system often land here or in purchased services.

fields.label: Unassigned costs
fields.summary: Costs not assigned to a department: building depreciation, building leases, and some interest.

fields.label: Salaries & wages
fields.summary: Pay for employees' time worked, including overtime and on-call premiums. Usually the largest expense.
drivers: Wage increases from union contracts and market pressure.
California's health care worker minimum wage (SB 525), phased in starting October 2024.
Headcount changes and shifts between employed and contract staff.

fields.label: Employee benefits
fields.summary: Paid time off, health insurance, retirement, workers' comp, and payroll taxes.
drivers: Health plan cost trends.
Pension actuarial changes, which can be large and one-time.

fields.label: Physician fees
fields.summary: Payments to physicians for professional services (e.g., ED coverage, hospitalists, call pay).
drivers: Physician coverage and stipend contracts, which have risen with specialist shortages.

fields.label: Other professional fees
fields.summary: Fees for non-physician professionals: consultants, auditors, lawyers, therapists, and registry (travel) nurses.
drivers: Travel/registry nurse spending, which spiked in 2021–22 and has come down since.
Consulting projects and legal matters.

fields.label: Supplies & drugs
fields.summary: Medical supplies, drugs, food, and office supplies.
drivers: Drug prices, especially specialty and oncology drugs.
Surgical volume and implant costs.
Supply-chain inflation.

fields.label: Purchased services
fields.summary: Outside vendors: imaging reads, equipment maintenance, collection agencies, IT, and management fees paid to a parent system.
drivers: Outsourcing (moves cost out of salaries into this line).
Changes in parent-system management fee allocations.

fields.label: Depreciation
fields.summary: The yearly cost of buildings and equipment spread over their useful life. A non-cash expense.
drivers: New buildings or equipment going into service (e.g., seismic replacement towers).
Older assets becoming fully depreciated.

fields.label: Leases & rentals
fields.summary: Rent for buildings, equipment, and leasehold improvements.

fields.label: Malpractice insurance
fields.summary: Professional liability insurance and actuarially determined self-insurance costs.

fields.label: Interest expense
fields.summary: Interest on short- and long-term debt.
drivers: New bond issues or refinancing.
Variable-rate debt when interest rates change (e.g., 2022–23 increases).

fields.label: All other expenses
fields.summary: Everything else: utilities, non-malpractice insurance, telephones, and other costs.

fields.label: Current assets
fields.summary: Cash, receivables, inventory, and other assets expected to turn into cash within a year.

fields.label: Limited-use assets
fields.summary: Cash and investments set aside by the board, a bond trustee, or others — e.g., funded depreciation or bond reserves.

fields.label: Net property & equipment
fields.summary: Land, buildings, and equipment at cost minus accumulated depreciation.

fields.label: Construction in progress
fields.summary: Cost of projects under construction that aren't in service yet.
drivers: Seismic compliance and expansion projects starting or finishing (completed projects move into property & equipment).

fields.label: Investments & other assets
fields.summary: Long-term investments and other non-current assets, including long-term amounts owed by affiliates.

fields.label: Intangible assets
fields.summary: Goodwill, unamortized financing costs, and other non-physical assets.

fields.label: Total assets
fields.summary: Everything the hospital owns. Equals total liabilities and equity.

fields.label: Current liabilities
fields.summary: Bills and obligations due within a year: accounts payable, accrued payroll, current debt payments.

fields.label: Deferred credits
fields.summary: Money received or recorded before it's earned, such as deferred third-party income.

fields.label: Long-term debt (net)
fields.summary: Debt due after one year, including long-term amounts owed to affiliates.

fields.label: Equity (net assets)
fields.summary: Total assets minus total liabilities — the hospital's net worth. Nonprofits call this fund balance or net assets.
fields.caution: Negative equity means liabilities exceed assets.

fields.label: Total liabilities & equity
fields.summary: Everything the hospital owes plus its equity. Equals total assets.

fields.label: Cash
fields.summary: Cash in the bank and immediately available, including savings, CDs, and treasury notes.
fields.caution: Many system-affiliated hospitals sweep cash to the parent daily, so hospital-level cash can be near zero even at financially strong systems.

fields.label: Patient accounts receivable
fields.summary: Unpaid patient bills owed by patients and insurers, at charges.

fields.hcaiLabel: Allowance for Uncollectible Receivables and Third Party Contractual Withholds
fields.label: Allowance for uncollectibles
fields.summary: The portion of receivables the hospital doesn't expect to collect.

fields.label: Buildings (at cost)
fields.summary: Original cost of buildings, parking structures, and fixed equipment.

fields.label: Equipment (at cost)
fields.summary: Original cost of movable and minor equipment.

fields.label: Total property & equipment (at cost)
fields.summary: Original cost of land, buildings, and equipment before depreciation.

fields.label: Accumulated depreciation
fields.summary: Total depreciation recorded to date on property and equipment. High relative to cost means aging facilities.

fields.label: Mortgages
fields.summary: Unpaid mortgage principal.

fields.label: Capital lease obligations
fields.summary: Unpaid principal on capital (finance) leases.

fields.label: Bonds payable
fields.summary: Unpaid principal on bonds.

fields.label: Total long-term debt
fields.summary: All long-term debt, including the portion due this year.

fields.label: Debt due within a year
fields.summary: The part of long-term debt that must be repaid in the next 12 months.

fields.label: Owed by affiliates
fields.summary: Amounts related organizations (e.g., the parent system) owe the hospital.
fields.caution: At system-affiliated hospitals this often holds the cash swept to the parent.

fields.label: Owed to affiliates
fields.summary: Amounts the hospital owes related organizations.

fields.label: Paid FTEs (employees)
fields.summary: Full-time-equivalent employees: total paid hours ÷ 2,080. Excludes registry and contract staff.

fields.hcaiLabel: Number of Nursing Service FTE Personnel
fields.label: Nursing FTEs
fields.summary: FTEs for nursing service personnel (RNs, LVNs, aides, orderlies, ward clerks), including registry nurses.

fields.label: Hours worked
fields.summary: Total hours actually worked, including contract staff.

fields.label: Paid time off hours
fields.summary: Paid hours not worked: vacation, sick leave, holidays.

fields.label: Total paid hours
fields.summary: All paid hours, worked or not.

fields.label: Active medical staff
fields.summary: Physicians who are voting members of the hospital's medical staff (employed or not).

fields.label: Residents & fellows (FTE)
fields.summary: Full-time-equivalent residents and fellows in training.

fields.label: Hours worked — Managers & supervisors
fields.summary: Administrators, directors, managers, and supervisors: hours actually worked by employees.

fields.label: Hours worked — Technical & specialist staff
fields.summary: Technologists, technicians, and other licensed or specialized roles: hours actually worked by employees.

fields.label: Hours worked — Registered nurses
fields.summary: Employed RNs providing direct patient care: hours actually worked by employees.

fields.label: Hours worked — Licensed vocational nurses
fields.summary: Employed LVNs providing direct patient care: hours actually worked by employees.

fields.label: Hours worked — Aides & orderlies
fields.summary: Nursing assistants, aides, and orderlies: hours actually worked by employees.

fields.hcaiLabel: Productive Hours Clerical and Other Administrative
fields.label: Hours worked — Clerical & administrative staff
fields.summary: Record-keeping, communication, and other administrative roles: hours actually worked by employees.

fields.hcaiLabel: Productive Hours Environmental and Food Services
fields.label: Hours worked — Environmental & food service staff
fields.summary: Housekeeping, dietary, maintenance, and security: hours actually worked by employees.

fields.hcaiLabel: Productive Hours All Other Employee Classifications
fields.label: Hours worked — All other employees
fields.summary: Salaried physicians, non-physician practitioners, and all other roles: hours actually worked by employees.

fields.label: Registry/travel nurse hours
fields.summary: Hours worked by registry or travel nursing staff (RNs, LVNs, aides) not on the hospital payroll.

fields.label: Other contract labor hours
fields.summary: Hours worked by other temporary contracted staff, such as therapists and clerical support.

fields.label: Hours worked — Inpatient units
fields.summary: Hours actually worked (employees plus contract staff) in nursing units and room & board for admitted patients.

fields.label: Hours worked — Ambulatory services
fields.summary: Hours actually worked (employees plus contract staff) in the ED, clinics, observation, and home health.

fields.label: Hours worked — Ancillary services
fields.summary: Hours actually worked (employees plus contract staff) in diagnostic and therapy departments: lab, imaging, pharmacy, surgery, therapy.

fields.label: Hours worked — Education & research
fields.summary: Hours actually worked (employees plus contract staff) in education and research programs.

fields.label: Hours worked — General services
fields.summary: Hours actually worked (employees plus contract staff) in dietary, laundry, housekeeping, and plant operations.

fields.label: Hours worked — Fiscal services
fields.summary: Hours actually worked (employees plus contract staff) in accounting, patient accounting, and admitting.

fields.label: Hours worked — Administration
fields.summary: Hours actually worked (employees plus contract staff) in administration, HR, medical records, and employee benefits.

fields.label: Hours worked — Non-operating departments
fields.summary: Hours actually worked (employees plus contract staff) in activities outside patient care, such as gift shops and medical office buildings.

fields.label: Paid hours — Inpatient units
fields.summary: All paid hours, including time off, in nursing units and room & board for admitted patients.

fields.label: Paid hours — Ambulatory services
fields.summary: All paid hours, including time off, in the ED, clinics, observation, and home health.

fields.label: Paid hours — Ancillary services
fields.summary: All paid hours, including time off, in diagnostic and therapy departments: lab, imaging, pharmacy, surgery, therapy.

fields.label: Paid hours — Education & research
fields.summary: All paid hours, including time off, in education and research programs.

fields.label: Paid hours — General services
fields.summary: All paid hours, including time off, in dietary, laundry, housekeeping, and plant operations.

fields.label: Paid hours — Fiscal services
fields.summary: All paid hours, including time off, in accounting, patient accounting, and admitting.

fields.label: Paid hours — Administration
fields.summary: All paid hours, including time off, in administration, HR, medical records, and employee benefits.

fields.label: Paid hours — Non-operating departments
fields.summary: All paid hours, including time off, in activities outside patient care, such as gift shops and medical office buildings.

metrics.label: Operating margin
metrics.summary: Cents of operating profit per dollar of operating revenue.
drivers: Volume and payment-rate changes (annual Medicare updates, commercial contract renegotiations).
Medi-Cal supplemental payments such as the Hospital Quality Assurance Fee program arrive in lumpy, multi-year cycles and can swing results sharply year to year.
Labor costs: the 2021–22 travel-nurse surge and California's health care worker minimum wage (SB 525, phased in from October 2024).
One-time items: COVID relief grants in 2020–21, prior-year cost report settlements.

metrics.label: Days cash on hand
metrics.summary: How many days the hospital could pay its operating expenses from the cash on its own balance sheet.
metrics.caution: Hospital-level cash only. System-affiliated hospitals often sweep cash to the parent, so compare within similar ownership structures. Rating-agency figures (which include investments at the system level) are much higher.
drivers: Operating results adding to or draining cash.
Cash swept to or from a parent system.
Timing of large receipts such as Medi-Cal supplemental payments.
Capital spending and debt service.

metrics.label: Occupancy rate
metrics.summary: Share of licensed beds filled on an average day.
metrics.formula: Patient days ÷ (licensed beds × days in period) — HCAI OCC_LIC
drivers: Occupancy moves with patient days (numerator) and bed counts (denominator) — a bed closure raises occupancy with no change in volume.
Length of stay rises when discharges to post-acute care are delayed or case mix gets sicker; it falls with care-management programs.

metrics.label: ED visits
metrics.summary: Emergency department visits in the year (annualized if the report didn't cover a full year).
drivers: ED volume swings with respiratory-virus seasons, the 2020 COVID drop, and nearby urgent-care or ED openings/closures.
Clinic volume moves with sites being added, sold, or moved to an affiliated medical group.

metrics.label: Net patient revenue
metrics.summary: What the hospital expects to collect for patient care after contractual discounts, charity care, and bad debt.
drivers: Volume and payment-rate changes (annual Medicare updates, commercial contract renegotiations).
Medi-Cal supplemental payments such as the Hospital Quality Assurance Fee program arrive in lumpy, multi-year cycles and can swing results sharply year to year.
Labor costs: the 2021–22 travel-nurse surge and California's health care worker minimum wage (SB 525, phased in from October 2024).
One-time items: COVID relief grants in 2020–21, prior-year cost report settlements.

metrics.label: Operating expense
metrics.summary: Total cost of running the hospital for the year, including depreciation and interest.
drivers: Volume and payment-rate changes (annual Medicare updates, commercial contract renegotiations).
Medi-Cal supplemental payments such as the Hospital Quality Assurance Fee program arrive in lumpy, multi-year cycles and can swing results sharply year to year.
Labor costs: the 2021–22 travel-nurse surge and California's health care worker minimum wage (SB 525, phased in from October 2024).
One-time items: COVID relief grants in 2020–21, prior-year cost report settlements.

metrics.label: Expense per adjusted discharge
metrics.summary: Operating cost per inpatient discharge, scaled up to count outpatient work — the standard unit-cost comparison between hospitals.
metrics.caution: Case mix matters: trauma, transplant, and tertiary centers treat sicker patients and cost more per discharge. Compare within similar hospitals.
drivers: Labor cost per hour (wage increases, travel and registry staff, SB 525 minimum wage).
Supply and drug costs, especially for surgery-heavy or oncology service lines.
Volume: fixed costs spread over fewer discharges push the unit cost up.
Charge-master changes move the outpatient adjustment, since it's based on gross charges.

metrics.label: Revenue per adjusted discharge
metrics.summary: Operating revenue per inpatient discharge, scaled up to count outpatient work. Compare with expense per adjusted discharge to see where the margin comes from.
drivers: Payer mix: Medicare and Medi-Cal pay less per case than commercial insurers.
Commercial contract renegotiations and annual Medicare rate updates.
Medi-Cal supplemental payments (Hospital Quality Assurance Fee program) arriving in lumpy cycles.
Case mix: sicker patients bring higher payments per discharge.

metrics.label: Outpatient visits
metrics.summary: Outpatient visits of every kind in the hospital's fiscal year, from the financial report (the utilization report doesn't total them).
metrics.caution: Counted by fiscal year, not calendar year like the other utilization measures. Hospitals count visits differently (a series of therapy sessions may be one visit or many), so compare trends more than levels.
drivers: ED volume swings with respiratory-virus seasons, the 2020 COVID drop, and nearby urgent-care or ED openings/closures.
Clinic volume moves with sites being added, sold, or moved to an affiliated medical group.

metrics.label: Payer mix
metrics.summary: Share of the hospital's business by payer, measured by gross charges (inpatient + outpatient) or by inpatient days.
metrics.formula: (GR_IP_<payer> + GR_OP_<payer>) ÷ Σ all payers; or DAY_<payer> ÷ Σ all payers
drivers: Admission volume: service-line growth, physician recruitment or departures, a competitor opening or closing.
Length of stay: delays discharging patients to skilled nursing or home care add days without adding patients.

Payer shifts: Medicare Advantage growth moves volume from Medicare fee-for-service to Medicare managed care; Medi-Cal enrollment swings (the 2023–24 end of continuous coverage, the 2024 expansion to undocumented adults) move volume between Medi-Cal, county programs, and self-pay.
Partial reporting periods (opening, closure, fiscal-year change) — check Days in Report Period.

metrics.label: Medicare margin
metrics.summary: Estimated profit or loss per dollar of Medicare net patient revenue, with Medicare's cost estimated from its charges and the hospital's cost-to-charge ratio.
metrics.formula: (NETRV_MCAR − GR_MCAR × TOT_OP_EXP ÷ (GR_PT_REV + OTH_OP_REV)) ÷ NETRV_MCAR, where MCAR = MCAR_TR + MCAR_MC and GR = GR_IP_ + GR_OP_
metrics.caution: Estimated, and more negative than MedPAC's figures by design. HCAI doesn't report expenses by payer, so Medicare's cost is its gross charges times the hospital's cost-to-charge ratio (the AHA payment-to-cost method). MedPAC's Medicare margin (−13% nationally in 2023) counts only Medicare-allowable costs from cost reports and only traditional Medicare. The AHA method counts all operating expense and includes Medicare Advantage: nationally it put Medicare at 82 cents per dollar of cost in 2022 (a margin near −22%), and California hospitals run lower, near 75 cents (about −33%). Compare hospitals with each other here, not with MedPAC or the Medicare cost report (CMS-2552).
drivers: Annual Medicare payment updates (IPPS and OPPS) versus local wage and supply inflation.
Case mix: sicker Medicare patients bring higher DRG payments.
Medicare Advantage contract terms, and denials or downgrades by MA plans.
Cost per case: length of stay, staffing, and supply use.

metrics.label: Medicare revenue per adjusted discharge
metrics.summary: Medicare net patient revenue per Medicare inpatient stay, scaled up for Medicare outpatient work.
metrics.formula: NETRV_MCAR ÷ (DIS_MCAR × GR_MCAR ÷ GR_IP_MCAR), where MCAR = MCAR_TR + MCAR_MC
drivers: Annual Medicare rate updates and the hospital's wage index.
Case mix index of Medicare patients.
Add-on payments: disproportionate share (DSH), uncompensated care, and graduate medical education.
Medicare Advantage rates, which are negotiated and can sit above or below traditional Medicare.

metrics.label: Medicare cost per adjusted discharge
metrics.summary: Estimated cost of caring for Medicare patients, per Medicare adjusted discharge.
metrics.formula: (GR_MCAR × TOT_OP_EXP ÷ (GR_PT_REV + OTH_OP_REV)) ÷ (DIS_MCAR × GR_MCAR ÷ GR_IP_MCAR), where MCAR = MCAR_TR + MCAR_MC
metrics.caution: Estimated, and more negative than MedPAC's figures by design. HCAI doesn't report expenses by payer, so Medicare's cost is its gross charges times the hospital's cost-to-charge ratio (the AHA payment-to-cost method). MedPAC's Medicare margin (−13% nationally in 2023) counts only Medicare-allowable costs from cost reports and only traditional Medicare. The AHA method counts all operating expense and includes Medicare Advantage: nationally it put Medicare at 82 cents per dollar of cost in 2022 (a margin near −22%), and California hospitals run lower, near 75 cents (about −33%). Compare hospitals with each other here, not with MedPAC or the Medicare cost report (CMS-2552).
drivers: Length of stay of Medicare patients.
Labor costs, contract labor, and supply prices.
Charge-master changes, which shift how expense is allocated between payers.

metrics.label: Medicare net patient revenue
metrics.summary: What the hospital expects to collect from traditional Medicare and Medicare Advantage plans, after contractual discounts.
drivers: Medicare volume and case mix.
Annual Medicare payment updates.
Prior-year cost report settlements, which can land in a later year.

metrics.label: Medicare Advantage share
metrics.summary: Share of the hospital's Medicare discharges covered by a Medicare Advantage (managed care) plan rather than traditional Medicare.
drivers: Medicare Advantage enrollment in the hospital's market, which has risen steadily in California.
Which MA plans the hospital is in network with.
Prior authorization and denial practices that steer MA patients elsewhere.

metrics.label: Medicare discharges
metrics.summary: Inpatient stays covered by traditional Medicare or Medicare Advantage in the hospital's fiscal year.
metrics.caution: From the financial report, so counted by fiscal year rather than the calendar years of the utilization report. Includes every inpatient unit, long-term care included.
drivers: Aging of the local population and Medicare enrollment.
The two-midnight rule and observation stays, which move Medicare patients between inpatient and outpatient.
Service line growth or closures (cardiac, orthopedics, oncology).

metrics.label: Medicare inpatient days
metrics.summary: Inpatient days for Medicare patients (traditional and Medicare Advantage) in the hospital's fiscal year.
metrics.caution: From the financial report (fiscal year). Includes long-term care and skilled nursing days, which the utilization report counts separately.
drivers: Medicare discharges and length of stay.
Discharge delays to skilled nursing facilities.
Distinct-part skilled nursing or sub-acute units.

metrics.label: Medicare average length of stay
metrics.summary: Average days a Medicare patient stays, across every inpatient unit.
metrics.caution: Includes long-term care and skilled nursing days, so hospitals with those units run much higher than their acute-care length of stay. The all-payer view is acute care only.
drivers: Discharge delays to skilled nursing and home health.
Case mix: older, sicker patients stay longer.
Long-term care or sub-acute units in the hospital.

metrics.label: Medicare outpatient visits
metrics.summary: Outpatient visits by Medicare patients (traditional and Medicare Advantage) in the hospital's fiscal year.
metrics.caution: Counted by fiscal year. Hospitals count visits differently, so compare trends more than levels.
drivers: Shift of procedures from inpatient to outpatient (CMS removing procedures from the inpatient-only list).
Observation stays, which count as outpatient under Medicare.
Outpatient clinic and imaging growth.
